name: Go and dance
subcategory: dance festival and camp booking marketplace
tagline: A booking marketplace for social dance festivals, congresses and dance holidays, with packages, passes and accommodation.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Revenue looks transaction based rather than a subscription, so there is no monthly figure to quote.

verdictSummary: The software here is a competent event catalogue with a checkout bolted on, and a coding agent can produce that shape in an afternoon. The thing you cannot produce is the inventory: hundreds of festivals and camps worldwide, with organizers who agreed to sell passes, rooms and packages through this specific pipe. You also cannot produce the payments, refunds and travel-adjacent customer service that sit behind a booking people fly for. A personal clone would be an empty shelf with a very nice shelf-bracket. What you can honestly build is a tracker for the events you already care about, which is a different and smaller product.
coreLoopDIY: A local dance event tracker that holds events you enter or import, tracks pass prices, deadlines and travel costs per trip, and shows a calendar plus a shortlist of what to book next.
requirements: Manual entry or ICS files for every event you want tracked
Optional per-site adapters if you want any automatic imports, and they will break
whatYouLose: The actual catalogue of festivals, camps and congresses, which is the entire point
Real booking: passes, hotel rooms and packages confirmed with the organizer
Payment handling, refunds and cancellation mess when a festival moves or dies
Discovery of events you had never heard of in cities you had not considered
Any leverage with organizers on pricing, early bird allocation or room blocks
moatNotes: Two-sided and seasonal: organizers list because dancers shop there, dancers shop there because organizers list. A clone starts cold on both sides, and nobody wires money to a stranger for a festival in another country.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because booking a dance trip is a bundle problem, not a search problem. You want a pass, a bed near the venue, dates that line up with flights, and some confidence the event is real and the money is recoverable. Assembling that yourself across organizer websites, half-dead Facebook events and hotel booking sites is a genuine chore, and a platform that already has the organizer relationships collapses it into one checkout. The software is replaceable; the agreements and the trust are not.
notes: The catalogue page is a weekend build; the catalogue is not. The moat is marketplace liquidity: organizer deals on one side, dancers who trust the checkout on the other.
prompt:
Build a local-only dance trip tracker. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite via sqlite3 (no ORM), Jinja2 templates server rendered, plain CSS in one file. Run with uvicorn on port 8000. Single repo, no Docker.

Data model:
- event: id, name, city, country, dance_styles (comma string), start_date, end_date, website_url, organizer_notes, status (watching | booked | skipped)
- pass_option: id, event_id, label (full pass, party pass, workshops only), price, currency, on_sale_until, booking_url
- trip_cost: id, event_id, kind (flight, lodging, transport, food, other), amount, currency, note
- deadline: id, event_id, label, due_date

Pages:
1. /  dashboard: next 90 days of events in date order, each row showing dates, city, cheapest pass price, total estimated trip cost, and the nearest deadline with days remaining. Rows turn amber when a deadline is inside 14 days and red when it has passed.
2. /events  full list with filters by status, country and dance style.
3. /events/new and /events/{id}/edit  forms covering the event plus inline add and remove of pass options, trip costs and deadlines.
4. /calendar  month grid with event blocks, pure HTML and CSS, no JS libraries.

Features that must work:
- Import events from an .ics file upload, mapping SUMMARY, DTSTART, DTEND, LOCATION and URL into an event row with status watching.
- Export all events as .ics.
- Currency conversion using a static rates table in config.py that I edit by hand. Do not call any exchange rate API. Show every total in a single base currency set in .env as BASE_CURRENCY.
- Seed script with three made up events so the UI is not empty on first run.

Explicitly out of scope: scraping any booking site, real payments, hotel search, flight search, user accounts, mobile app, notifications beyond on-page colour coding.

Deliver: README with setup commands, .env.example containing BASE_CURRENCY only, requirements.txt, seed.py, and a smoke test that creates an event, adds a pass and a deadline, and asserts the dashboard renders it.
